title: ～は別として — “aside from ～ / setting ～ aside”
summary: Puts one thing aside as a separate matter and talks about the rest. It follows a noun (or a noun-like phrase) and then the main point is stated. Used for “set X aside, then Y”, or “X may be different, but Y is …”.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形／名詞（疑問詞＋か）＋かは別として

body.h: Treating it as a separate issue
body.p: A は別として、B means “whatever A is, B is what matters or what I will say.” It does not deny A; it just sets it aside for now. 値段は別として、デザインは気に入った: price is another question, but I like the design.
A fixed phrase 冗談は別として (joking aside) is used to return to the main subject. 結果は別として shows that the process matters more than the result. A can also be a clause: 本当かどうかは別として.
～はさておき is very similar and a little more written. ～はともかく also sets A aside, but with the sense that A is less important. ～は別として is the most neutral.

examples.ja: 値段（ねだん）は別（べつ）として、デザインは気（き）に入（い）った。
examples.romaji: Nedan wa betsu toshite, dezain wa ki ni itta.
examples.tr: Aside from the price, I like the design.

examples.ja: 冗談（じょうだん）は別（べつ）として、そろそろ本題（ほんだい）に入（はい）ろう。
examples.romaji: Joudan wa betsu toshite, sorosoro hondai ni hairou.
examples.tr: Joking aside, let’s get to the main topic now.

examples.ja: 結果（けっか）は別（べつ）として、最後（さいご）まで頑張（がんば）ったことが大事（だいじ）だ。
examples.romaji: Kekka wa betsu toshite, saigo made ganbatta koto ga daiji da.
examples.tr: Aside from the result, what matters is that you tried until the end.

pitfalls: It does not mean “A is unimportant”. It only sets A aside for now. For “A matters less”, ～はともかく fits better.
A must be a noun or a noun-like phrase (verbs need こと or か: 行くかどうかは別として).
